proof.text:
Write $r=a_{\mathrm{et},*}$, $s=a_{\mathrm{proet},*}$, $R_T=\nu_{T,*}$, and let $\eta_T,\epsilon_T$ be the comparison adjunction units and counits. Restriction gives $R_Ps=rR_Z$: on an etale object $V\to P$ both sides evaluate a pro-etale sheaf at $Z\times_PV$. This is an identity on sections, restrictions and scalar actions, by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For an etale module sheaf $H$ the underived restriction mate $b_H:A_PrH\to sA_ZH$ is the adjunct of $r(\eta_{Z,H}):rH\to rR_ZA_ZH=R_PsA_ZH$. Expanding the adjunction formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives
$$b_H=\epsilon_{P,sA_ZH}\circ A_P(r\eta_{Z,H}),\qquad R_P(b_H)\circ\eta_{P,rH}=r(\eta_{Z,H}).$$
Indeed the second equality follows by naturality of $\eta_P$ at $r\eta_{Z,H}$ followed by $R_P(\epsilon_{P,N})\circ\eta_{P,R_PN}=1$ at $N=sA_ZH$. Thus it holds for the specified mate, with no choice of an isomorphism.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections] with affine base $P$ and the constant one-object presentation $P=P$. The comparison unit at $P$ identifies $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ with $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proet}},A_PB)$ for every etale module sheaf $B$. Evaluate the second equation of step 1 at the terminal object $P$ and take $B=rH$. Under this unit identification, $\Gamma(P,b_H)$ is exactly
$$\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{et}},H)\xrightarrow{\eta_{Z,H}(Z)}\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A_ZH).$$
Here $R_P$ and $R_Z$ are restriction, so their values at $P$ and $Z$ are the same sections, respectively. The map $\eta_{Z,H}(Z)$ is the inverse-image section map by the inverse-image adjunction. All maps commute with morphisms $H\to H'$, since they are components of natural transformations. Applying this calculation to each $I^n$ gives an equality of cochain maps, because naturality also applies to every differential $I^n\to I^{n+1}$.

proof.text:
Let $Q$ denote the appropriate localization functor, and $\alpha^r_L:Q(rL)\to Rr(QL)$ and $\alpha^s_M:Q(sM)\to Rs(QM)$ the right-derived units. The fixed construction [def-weil-pbc-fixed-derived-comparisons] is obtained by extending $Q(b_L)$ followed by $\alpha^s_{A_ZL}$. The universal-property factorization in clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] therefore gives, suppressing the natural exact-functor localization isomorphisms,
$$\beta_{a,QL}\circ A_P(\alpha^r_L)=\alpha^s_{A_ZL}\circ Q(b_L).$$
At $L=I$, clause (2) makes $\alpha^r_I$ invertible, since $I$ is bounded below and termwise injective. This determines the actual $\beta_{a,F}$ in the source model $QA_PrI$. This is precisely the defining factorization of rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange, rather than an identification based on invertibility of its endpoints.

proof.text:
Naturality of the right-derived unit $\alpha^s$ at $j:A_ZI\to J$ gives
$$Rs(Qj)\circ\alpha^s_{A_ZI}=\alpha^s_J\circ Q(sj).$$
The morphism $Qj$ is invertible by the assumed quasi-isomorphism; $\alpha^s_J$ is invertible by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Consequently, using $\alpha^s_J$ and $Rs(Qj)$ for the canonical identification of $Rs(A_ZF)$ with $Q(sJ)$, the equality of step 3 represents $\beta_{a,F}$ by the cochain map
$$A_PrI\xrightarrow{b_I}sA_ZI\xrightarrow{sj}sJ.$$
No acyclicity or injectivity of $A_ZI$ is assumed. The models are the bounded-below resolution models of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; their passage to the unbounded categories is part of the fixed comparison definition.

source.place: (3), direct-image resolution models and compatibility with the derived units

proof.text: The field $\Omega$ is w-contractible in [sk-def-pe-wlocal]: its spectrum and its component space are singletons, so the closed-point condition and extremal disconnectedness hold. Its only maximal localization is $\Omega$, which is strictly henselian: the residue field is algebraically closed, hence separably closed, and the henselian condition for $(\Omega,0)$ says that idempotents of $B/0=B$ lift uniquely to $B$, an identity, by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Thus [det-pe-wc-sections-exact], with $X=U=P$ and the constant coefficient ring sheaf, gives exactness of $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proet}},-)$. Etale point sections are exact for every $\Lambda$ by clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk]. These exact functors may be applied termwise in the derived categories by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Apply pro-etale point sections to step 4. Direct-image evaluation at $P$ is evaluation at $Z$ on each site. Step 2 now makes the resulting cochain map exactly $\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{et}},I)\to\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A_ZI)\to\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},J)$, with second map $\Gamma(j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] applied to the two module-section functors, $I$ and $J$ compute the respective derived global sections.

source.place: (1), (2), and (3): exact point sections and the two section complexes

proof.text:
It remains to check the specified cohomology comparison. The exact adjunction $A_Z\dashv R_Z$ has right adjoint preserving injectives by [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives]. Hence $R_ZJ$ is a bounded-below injective complex, so it computes $RR_Z(A_ZF)$. The cochain map
$$k=R_Z(j)\circ\eta_{Z,I}:I\longrightarrow R_ZJ$$
is adjoint to $j:A_ZI\to J$. The explicit derived-adjunction bijection of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], applied with the exact left functor $G=A_Z$ and right functor $F=R_Z$, therefore identifies $Qk$ with the derived unit at $F$: in its formula take the left resolution to be the identity, the right resolution to be $j$, and the representing adjunct to be $j$. After the target identification $QJ\simeq A_ZF$, this adjunct is the identity, which characterizes the unit. Its hypotheses hold at $K=A_ZI$, $M=I$: by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] (2) $J$ is K-injective, so by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] every quasi-isomorphism $s:A_ZI\to I_s$ has a map $g_s:I_s\to J$, unique up to homotopy, with $Q(g_s)=Q(j)Q(s)^{-1}$ (so $g_j\simeq1$); thus $s\mapsto Q(R_ZI_s)$ is essentially constant with value $Q(R_ZJ)$, $j_0=j$, $p_s=Q(R_Zg_s)$, and $p_j$ is the identity. As $A_Z$ is exact, $t\mapsto Q(A_ZP)$ is essentially constant with value $Q(A_ZI)$ and $u_{\mathrm{id}}=1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] (2) this value is $RR_Z(A_ZF)$. Applying etale derived sections to $Qk$ is represented by $\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{et}},k)$ since $I$ and $R_ZJ$ are injective complexes. Restriction gives $\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{et}},R_ZJ)=\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},J)$ termwise. Consequently this is precisely the cochain map in step 5. This computes both the derived unit and the final-object composition comparison on the same injective complex; the resulting morphism is the canonical cohomology comparison of [sk-prop-sf-comparison].

The left side is natural in $F$, since the fixed derived comparison is a natural transformation and point sections are functorial; the inverse-image section map is also natural. For explicit resolution independence, let $I',j':A_ZI'\to J'$ be another choice for the same $F$. These bounded-below complexes of injectives are K-injective by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]; the module categories have enough injectives, as [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution] applied to a single sheaf in degree 0 embeds it in an injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the canonical source identification is represented by a homotopy equivalence $u:I\to I'$, and the target identification by a homotopy equivalence $v:J\to J'$. Choose their homotopy classes to represent the identities on $F$ and $A_ZF$. Then $vj$ and $j'A_Zu$ have the same image in the derived category. The same Hom-bijection, now for maps from $A_ZI$ into $J'$, says that these cochain maps are homotopic. Naturality of the inverse-image section map, followed by this homotopy, gives the commutative resolution-comparison square after localization. Additive section functors preserve the homotopy equations termwise. Thus the displayed map is independent of both resolutions under their canonical derived identifications. The same argument for a morphism $F\to F'$ proves the asserted naturality on any resolution representatives.

title: Resolution-level pro-étale section map
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\Lambda$ an arbitrary discrete commutative ring, and $a:Z\to P$ a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves of value $\Lambda$ and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For $F\in D^+(Z_{\Et},\Lambda)$, let $I$ be a bounded below complex of injective etale module sheaves representing $F$, and let $j:A_ZI\to J$ be a quasi-isomorphism to a bounded below complex of injective pro-etale module sheaves [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. Let
$$\beta_{a,F}:A_PRa_{\Et,*}F\longrightarrow Ra_{\mathrm{proét},*}A_ZF$$
be precisely the fixed derived underived restriction mate [def-weil-pbc-fixed-derived-comparisons], whose invertibility is [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]. Use the resolution models for direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the point-section identification $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proét}},A_PH)=\Gamma(P_{\Et},H)$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections], and exactness of point sections [det-pe-wc-sections-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk]. Under these identifications, applying point sections to $\beta_{a,F}$ gives precisely the morphism represented by
$$\Gamma(Z_{\Et},I)\longrightarrow\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},A_ZI)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(j)}\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},J),$$
where the first arrow takes each section to its inverse-image section. Thus it is the canonical cohomology comparison $R\Gamma(Z_{\Et},F)\to R\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},A_ZF)$ of [sk-prop-sf-comparison], not just some isomorphism between those objects. The equality is natural in $F$ and is independent of the resolutions under their canonical derived identifications [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived].
